Subject: Vaulted CA & Private DNS consent — roadmap and action items

Hi Jared / Barnes SecOps,

Thanks again for the time earlier today. As discussed, we want to lay out a minimal-risk, auditable path for running Redwood Private in your VPC while letting Barnes retain control of private TLS material (vaulted CA / HSM). This thread captures the recommended options, proposed change windows, and the consent/proof steps we need from your side.

Top-level options (we recommend Option B for most customers):

- Option A — Bring-your-own cert (Upload): Barnes signs a CA bundle and securely uploads a PKCS#12 to the Redwood Private control plane. Redwood installs into the on-prem agent; rotation requires re-upload. Pros: simple model, full customer control. Cons: manual rotation, requires secure workflow for uploads.

- Option B — Vaulted CSR + remote signing (recommended): Redwood generates CSRs inside your VPC/on-prem agent and forwards them to your HSM signing endpoint (signed CSRs are returned). Rotations are automated; Redwood never holds the private key. Pros: automated rotation, least-privilege. Cons: requires a small signing endpoint or an HSM-facing API on your side.

- Option C — ACME puller with ephemeral leaf certs: On-prem ACME client pulls ephemeral certs; Redwood validates via DNS/HTTP challenge. Pros: zero long-term cert storage. Cons: requires DNS automation for private zones.

DNS proof & ownership options we discussed: TXT proof in private zone (preferred), zone-aware ACME (if you can permit the puller IP), or pre-provisioned CNAME delegation to a Redwood-managed shadow zone.

Requested deliverables from Barnes to proceed:
- Which option do you prefer (A/B/C)?
- Access pattern for signing: (mutual TLS endpoint / signed CSR via S3)
- DNS method chosen for proof-of-ownership (TXT / ACME / delegation)
- Preferred rotation cadence and emergency rotation SLA (e.g., 30 days, 7 days emergency)

Attachments: vaulted-ca-integration-diagram.png (system diagram), dns-proof-checklist.xlsx (detailed steps).

If you agree, we’ll schedule a 60-minute technical runthrough Thursday and prepare a follow-up playbook and DocuSign consent for the one-click delegation we discussed.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Kim,

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers and a few follow-ups from our side:

1) Prefer Option B (vaulted CSR + remote signing). We want automated rotation without giving Redwood persistent access to private keys.
2) Our HSM team prefers an mTLS-protected signing endpoint that accepts PKCS#10 and returns signed certs. We can stand that up in the next sprint.
3) DNS: We run an internal Route 53 private zone. TXT proof is the easiest for us; ACME DNS in private zones is possible but needs change windows.
4) Rotation cadence: standard 90-day, emergency rotation within 24 hours.

Two questions:
- How will the on-prem agent authenticate to Redwood control plane for orchestration (we prefer short-lived tokens tied to our KMS)?
- Can Redwood support a ‘recovery-only’ path where, if the signing endpoint is unreachable, Redwood temporarily falls back to issuing a short-lived leaf cert from Redwood-managed ephemeral CA for up to 48 hours? We want an explicit audit trail for fallback issuance.

On the last point — we need clear policy on what triggers fallback and an automatic rollback to customer-signed certs.

Regards,
Jared Liu
Sr. Security Engineer — Barnes Analytics

Jared / Kim,

Thanks for the clarifications — we can support the patterns Jared outlined. A few implementation notes and a proposed default:

Implementation notes:
- Authentication: the on-prem agent will use short-lived client certs minted by Barnes KMS (via SVID-like flow) to authenticate to the Redwood control channel. We will accept a signed JWT from Barnes STS as well; both options provide auditable issuance.
- Signing endpoint: Redwood's CSR flow expects a PKCS#10 over mTLS; response is the leaf cert + chain. The agent will store only the leaf key if the private key is generated inside the agent (preferred).
- Fallback issuance: we can implement a fallback policy that issues a short-lived (48-hour) leaf cert signed by Redwood's ephemeral CA under the following conditions: (1) signing endpoint returns repeated failures > 10m, (2) customer consents to emergency fallback in DocuSign, and (3) an explicit audit event is generated and pushed to your SIEM via webhook. Fallback will be limited to specific FQDNs you pre-declare.

Proposed defaults (we can change on the runbook):
- CSR rotation flow: automated, rotate leaf certs every 90 days; renew within 7 days of expiry.
- Emergency rotation SLA: attempt auto-rotation within 5 minutes; if signing endpoint unavailable for >10 minutes escalate to on-call and start fallback window.
- DNS proof: TXT in private zone; agent will poll TTL and verify once visible from within VPC.

Action items for next week:
- Barnes: stand up an mTLS signing endpoint and provide a test client cert for the on-prem agent.
- Redwood: prepare a test agent image and a small PKI-runbook with step-by-step CSR exchange, plus the DocuSign consent template for emergency fallback.

I'll draft a minimal runbook and share a test checklist by EOD.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Folks — thanks, this is shaping up well. Attached is a first-draft runbook (runbook-vaulted-cert-rotation.md) and an updated diagram that includes the fallback flow. Key decisions we have from this thread:

- Path chosen: Option B (vaulted CSR + remote signing).
- DNS proof: TXT record in Barnes private Route 53 zone; Redwood agent will poll with exponential backoff.
- Auth: short-lived certs minted by Barnes KMS for agent authentication; we will accept an STS-signed JWT as alternate.
- Fallback: Redwood ephemeral 48-hour cert allowed only with signed consent; audit events and webhook to Barnes SIEM required.

Next steps / ownership:

- Redwood (Karthik): drop a test agent image and a step-by-step CSR exchange checklist in the shared Drive by Friday 12/11.
